subject: Pre-sales: workload cadence & GPU-tilt questionnaire
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Lim <andrew@fluxlabs.ai>, Katie Moreno <katie@fluxlabs.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-sales: workload cadence & GPU-tilt questionnaire

Andrew / Katie —

Thanks for the demo earlier. To size a dedicated pool and recommend a GPU mix we need a short intake that captures cadence and prompt/response characteristics. Can you fill the bullets below (or attach a sample CSV) by EOD Tuesday? If easier, a high-level estimate is fine — we can refine in the sizing workshop.

Quick asks:
- Peak and baseline RPS (API calls per second) and preferred timezone for peak (e.g., US-EAST morning).
- Typical concurrency per user session and expected session duration (avg/min/max).
- Prompt length distribution (percent of calls at <64, 64–256, 256–1024 tokens) and average response length in tokens.
- % of calls that use streaming vs full-response.
- Sidecar work: embeddings/rerank usage per 1k requests (if any).
- SLA target (p99 latency target for user-facing requests) and acceptable cold-start window.
- Any planned growth window (e.g., 3x campaign spike in Nov) and committed burst behavior.

If you have an anonymized traffic sample, please attach (we accept CSV with timestamp, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, outcome). I’ve attached a one-page template.

Goal on our side: come back with a recommended fleet (GPU SKUs + counts), expected P99 latency at target load, and a fallback routing plan for burst days.

Thanks —
Jordan

Subject: Re: Pre-sales: workload cadence & GPU-tilt questionnaire

Jordan —

Thanks, sending a quick pass here. I attached a small sample (anonymized). High-level numbers below — happy to expand.

- Baseline RPS: 12 rps (US-PST daytime)
- Peak RPS: 220 rps (we expect ~10–15 minute campaign bursts occasionally)
- Concurrency per user session: avg 2 concurrent prompts; session duration typically 30–90s
- Prompt length distribution: ~55% <64 tokens, 30% 64–256, 15% 256–1024
- Average response length: 140 tokens
- Streaming: ~40% of calls request streaming
- Sidecar: embeddings for search ≈ 120 embeddings per 1k requests; rerank occurs on ~8% of sessions
- SLA target: p99 <= 350ms for simple prompts; p99 <= 800ms acceptable for heavier completion workflows
- Growth/campaigns: expect 4x sustained growth around product launch (Q4) with short spikes ~8x for marketing pushes

Notes: we currently use a mix of open models and a tuned finetune for summarization which increases average response length and KV cache needs. We can share a sample of anonymized traces (attached flux_traffic_sample.csv).

— Andrew
Andrew Lim
Head of ML Ops | FluxLabs
andrew@fluxlabs.ai

Subject: Re: Pre-sales: workload cadence & GPU-tilt questionnaire

Thanks Andrew — this is great and gives us enough to start. Sharing with Marissa for GPU-mix guidance and a draft sizing. A couple follow-ups to make the sizing defensible:

1) Can you confirm the average token ratio (prompt:response) for the 15% heavy bucket? If KV cache hits are common for your summarization flows, please add hit-rate estimate.
2) For the 8% rerank flows, are you running pairwise rerank (n^2) or single-pass scoring? Approx n (candidates) would help.
3) Any hard constraints on cold-start (is 3s startup okay for non-interactive batch?), and do you prefer reserved capacity for steady baseline or just commit for peak windows?

We’ll produce a 3-option sizing: minimal committed baseline (cost optimized), balanced (good p99 headroom + reserved burst), and aggressive (low-latency, more GPU count). Plan to include suggested quantization and cache sizing.

Best —
Jordan

Subject: Fwd: Pre-sales: workload cadence & GPU-tilt questionnaire

Folks — forwarding with preliminary sizing notes. Quick read: we should propose a hybrid pool for FluxLabs (A100x4 style for KV-heavy summarization + L40x2 for high-concurrency, cost-sensitive baseline). Rationale bullets below.

Sizing highlights (draft):
- Baseline committed: 6 x L40 (good for sustained 12 rps + modest concurrency with quantization)
- Burst pool (reserved + autoscale): add 8 x A100-style nodes to cover 220 rps campaign bursts while keeping p99 ~300–500ms depending on prompt mix
- KV cache: targeting 60–70% hit rate with prefix caching for summarization flows; design cache nodes with 256GB host RAM per GPU group
- Streaming: ensure streaming-tail optimization (reduce transformer tail latency) — recommend routing streaming requests to low-occupancy GPUs during peak
- Rerank: n approximately 12 candidates — use batch scoring on the burst pool to avoid latency hit on baseline nodes

Ask: Andrew, can you confirm KV hit-rate estimate and whether rerank n is closer to 8–12? Also confirm if FluxLabs prefers predictable monthly reserved cost vs commit-to-peak only during launch.

Notes: attaching our one-page SLO worksheet (slo_requirements.pdf) and will follow with a short deck.

—Marissa
